memory_candidates.content: When validating/normalizing a comma-joined-vs-single-author-name ambiguity (e.g. 'Last, First' vs packed 'First Last, First Last, ...'), a robust heuristic is: flag as multi-author-joined only if a string contains 2+ ', ' occurrences, OR exactly one ', ' followed by 2+ non-initial capitalized tokens (regex [A-Z][a-zA-Z]+, at least 2 chars) in the remainder. This correctly distinguishes 'Gabbay, Dov M.' (single author, initial after comma) from 'Patrick Blackburn, Maarten de Rijke' (two authors) without false positives, verified against a 270-entry real corpus.

This repo's doc-lint (.claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh) requires any script referenced from an extension's SKILL.md/agent docs to be (a) listed in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array AND (b) physically present on disk under .claude/extensions/{ext}/scripts/, in addition to any canonical copy under .claude/scripts/. Both are required or the extension FAILs the lint.

When a task's scope explicitly forbids writing to an external/sibling repo (e.g. ~/Projects/Literature), verify non-mutation empirically at each step (md5sum of the specific files read, git status/diff content review to rule out pre-existing unrelated dirty state from a separate project sharing the same directory tree) rather than assuming read-only tool usage was sufficient. Sibling repos can have their own independent .claude/ Claude Code config that coincidentally resembles the current repo's files.
